strengths: Well-motivated problem with compelling empirical evidence of computational redundancy and history-agnostic limitations in dLLM parallel decoding (Figures 1, 3)
Practical, training-free solution that requires no architectural changes and is orthogonal to other inference optimizations (KV cache, Early Stop, PyTorch compiler, FP8 quantization)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 benchmarks, 2 dLLM models, with thorough ablations on hyperparameters, block length, and generation length up to 4K
Strong and consistent speedups (5.48× on LLaDA-8B-Instruct, 4.11× on LLaDA-MoE) with minimal overall accuracy loss (+0.48 and +0.15 average)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations that communicate both problem and solution mechanisms
Detailed reproducibility details, publicly available models, and explicit hyperparameter specifications
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core idea is exponential decay with power transformation of top-1 logits, representing incremental rather than foundational advance
Lack of theoretical justification for design choices (why power transformation γ<1? why this accumulation scheme? why block-level credits?) without principled grounding or convergence analysis
Hyperparameter sensitivity without guidance: three hyperparameters (α, β, γ) require tuning with dataset-dependent optimal values; selected α=0.65, β=0.7 appear arbitrary
Inconsistent performance improvements: often marginal (0.15 on MoE), sometimes negative (LCB -0.61, KorBench CD* -0.24), with no statistical significance testing despite these small differences
Superficial analysis of when/why method works: Figure 6 explanation of GSM8K vs. HumanEval differences is insufficient; no predictive framework for task applicability
Missing computational overhead analysis: no measurement of memory or compute cost of credit maintenance despite efficiency being core motivation
Limited model scope: evaluation only on LLaDA family (8B and MoE scales); generalization to other dLLM architectures unclear
Block-level credit design choice lacks justification: significant architectural constraint presented without analysis of information loss or cross-block alternatives
Experimental deviations from original papers: authors acknowledge settings may differ from LLaDA/LLaDA-MoE papers without fully characterizing impact
Underexplored CD* variant: higher performance (+0.49, +0.36) but 10% lower speed; no clear guidance on variant selection for practitioners

strengths: Well-motivated problem analysis with clear empirical evidence (Figures 1, 3) showing gaps between token stabilization and actual decoding
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks and 2 dLLM backbones with consistent methodology
Practical training-free approach with demonstrated orthogonality to existing optimizations (Early Stop, KV-cache, PyTorch Compiler, FP8 quantization)
Solid empirical work including hyperparameter ablations (Figure 7), block length analysis (Figure 8), and scalability testing to 4K sequences
Reproducibility effort: publicly available models, detailed configurations, clear algorithmic description, TPF metric robustness
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core mechanism (Eq. 6) is straightforward exponential moving average with power transformation—engineering optimization rather than fundamental NLP contribution

Critical missing comparison: Wang et al. (2025) on temporal dynamics appears highly relevant but lacks detailed experimental comparison; no comparison with other history-aware dLLM acceleration methods
Weak theoretical justification: specific form of credit accumulation (Eq. 6), concave transformation (p^γ), and log-domain fusion (Eq. 7) lack rigorous justification beyond intuition
Inconsistent performance gains: +0.48 average improvement with notable degradation on key benchmarks (GSM8K: -0.76, LiveCodeBench: -0.61), contradicting universal improvement claims
Fundamental limitations not addressed: paper acknowledges performance issues on reasoning tasks but provides no solution, raising concerns about method applicability
Ad-hoc design choices: block-level credit restriction contradicts historical information motivation; three hyperparameters (α, β, γ) for 'training-free' method with γ never ablated
No statistical rigor: missing error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing for improvements often within ±0.5-1.0 point noise margins
Insufficient ablation studies: no component ablations, no analysis of what credits capture, no comparison of alternative fusion mechanisms vs. log-domain addition
Incomplete experimental reporting: Early Stop behavior varies across sections with acknowledged significant TPF impact; some configurations 'slightly deviate' from original papers

strengths: Clear empirical motivation: Excellent analysis (Figures 1, 3, 6) quantifying the temporal gap between token stabilization and actual decoding in dLLMs
Practical and elegant solution: Training-free, plug-and-play method requiring only logit modifications with no architectural changes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Eight diverse benchmarks, two model families, significant speedups (5.48× on LLaDA-8B, 4.11× on LLaDA-MoE) with detailed ablation studies
Strong orthogonality: Demonstrated compatibility with multiple acceleration techniques (KV caching, early stopping, PyTorch compilation, FP8 quantization) with consistent gains
Thorough hyperparameter analysis: Detailed ablation on α and β (Section 5.3) and block length sensitivity (Appendix C.3) provides practical guidance
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is straightforward logit accumulation via exponential moving average and log-domain fusion—standard techniques applied to dLLMs without fundamental innovation

Insufficient theoretical justification: No convergence analysis, theoretical guarantees, or formal derivation of key claims (e.g., multiplicative equivalence in Eq. 7); choice of γ<1 motivated only intuitively

Inconsistent accuracy results: Substantial task-specific degradation masked by averaging (GSM8K: -0.76, LCB: -0.61), contradicting uniform improvement claims; no statistical significance testing or multi-run results

Hyperparameter selection concerns: Fixed α=0.65, β=0.7 based on 5 datasets but applied to 8; Figure 7 shows substantial variance, and optimal values appear dataset-dependent without principled selection guidance for new tasks

Confounded experimental design: Early stop enablement significantly affects results (noted but not controlled); block length choice (64) appears somewhat arbitrary; limited baselines (only Fast-dLLM and vanilla LLaDA; no comparison with concurrent temporal methods like Wang et al. 2025)
Questionable scalability claims: Performance at 4K tokens shows significant degradation comparable to baseline; practical utility for long sequences unclear despite scalability section
Block-level design limitation: Credits maintained only within current decoding block, limiting ability to leverage long-range historical dependencies; justification is weak

Missing analysis of failure modes: Paper doesn't adequately explain why method underperforms on GSM8K (-0.76) while excelling on HumanEval (+3.04), or provide guidance on when to apply/avoid CreditDecoding

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear empirical demonstration of computational redundancy in dLLM parallel decoding; identifies concrete gap between early prediction and late decoding
Sound methodology with theoretical grounding (Eq. 4-5 deriving minimum gain) and practical design; EMA-based credit accumulation balances global decay and focused enhancement interpretably

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks (knowledge, reasoning, coding, understanding) and 5 dLLM architectures (8B-100B scale); thorough ablation studies and scalability analysis to 4K token lengths

Strong empirical results with 5.48× speedup and +0.48 accuracy on primary model; consistent improvements across diverse architectures; orthogonality verified across KV cache, compilation, quantization optimizations
Practical design enabling plug-and-play deployment without retraining; tuning-free adaptive variant improves usability; clear presentation with excellent visualizations of decoding boundaries
Excellent reproducibility with publicly available models, detailed configurations, and extensive supplementary analysis; honest documentation of limitations and failure modes
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty; applies standard EMA-based temporal averaging to dLLM context rather than introducing fundamental new techniques; primarily an engineering optimization
Concerning performance degradation on reasoning-intensive tasks (GSM8K -0.76, MATH -0.06); suggests method unsuitable for important task categories; adaptive variant provides only marginal mitigation

Fundamental applicability limitations: method requires sufficient denoising steps and less effective for aggressive parallel decoding or pure-diffusion dLLMs with small block sizes; reduces generality

Misleading 'tuning-free' framing: method has three hyperparameters tuned on LLaDA-8B-Instruct; adaptive variant achieves only 11-25% TPF vs 27% with tuning; generalization to new models/datasets unclear
Single-run results without error bars or confidence intervals; no statistical significance testing despite small accuracy gains on some benchmarks; insufficient for rigorous claims
Limited architecture diversity: all evaluations on LLaDA family and variants within same ecosystem; generalization to fundamentally different dLLM designs (Dream, Seed Diffusion) unverified

Dataset-dependent denoising traces (Figure 13) reveal fundamentally different confidence dynamics across tasks; limited guidance on identifying when method will succeed; suggests high task-specificity
Block-wise credit accumulation restriction justified only for unquantified 'efficiency'; impact on potential speedups unclear; cross-block credit tracking cost never analyzed

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear empirical evidence of the prediction-decoding temporal gap (Figures 3-5)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 dLLM architectures, 8 benchmarks, with extensive ablations on hyperparameters and scalability
Practical training-free method that integrates cleanly with existing optimizations and shows strong primary results (5.48× speedup with +0.48 accuracy on LLaDA-8B)
Detailed reproducibility materials including algorithms, hyperparameters, and supplementary experiments
Tuning-free adaptive variant provided to improve usability (Section 4.3)
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: the core mechanism (EMA-based trace credit + log-fused logits) is straightforward engineering without significant methodological advancement
Inadequately addressed performance degradation on reasoning-intensive tasks (GSM8K -0.76, MATH -0.06, LCB -0.61), which the authors only acknowledge but do not resolve
Insufficient theoretical justification for key design choices: why EMA specifically? Why log(C+1) fusion form? Why these functional forms without ablations on alternatives?
Misleading 'training-free' claim: limitations section admits hyperparameter tuning is still required on validation sets, contradicting the main value proposition
Inconsistent generalization across dLLM paradigms: 3-4× speedup difference between Pure Diffusion (7.00×) and Block Diffusion (1.91×) variants indicates limited applicability
Critical limitation under Top-K decoding: TPF cannot improve when decode counts are fixed (Table 3), severely limiting real-world applicability
Single-run results without error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; no variance analysis despite hyperparameter sensitivity
Block-level confinement of the method (Section 4.2) limits applicability but is not ablated or justified; magnitude of sacrificed speedup unclear
Appendix C.5 analysis suggests primary speedup source is improved context rather than trace credit mechanism itself, but this dynamic is underdeveloped
Strong dataset-dependency (Appendix C.6, Figure 13) with different confidence trajectories across tasks, yet hyperparameters fixed to maximize average performance

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear visualization of the prediction-decoding gap (Figures 3-5)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 benchmarks, multiple architectures (8B-100B parameters), and extensive ablations
Strong empirical results: 5.48× speedup with +0.48 accuracy improvement, achieving both speed and performance gains simultaneously
Practical and deployable: training-free, plug-and-play design orthogonal to existing optimizations (KV cache, quantization, compilers)
Rigorous experimental methodology with clear documentation, ablation studies, and honest discussion of limitations and failure modes
Effective analysis of temporal consistency in confidence trajectories (Figure 4) supporting the core hypothesis
Tuning-free adaptive variant (Section 4.3) improves usability while maintaining competitive performance
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution combines standard EMA accumulation (Eq. 6) and logit fusion (Eq. 7) without fundamental methodological innovation
Significant performance degradation on reasoning-intensive tasks (GSM8K -0.76, MATH -0.06, DROP -0.08) with no proposed mitigation strategy
Hyperparameter sensitivity despite 'training-free' framing: three hyperparameters (α, β, γ) require tuning with dataset-dependent optima (Figures 6-7)
Limited model diversity in evaluation: primarily LLaDA variants; only 5 models tested in Table 2, missing Dream, SEED, and other dLLM families
Block Diffusion models (SDAR, LLaDA2) show substantially smaller gains (1.83-2.68×) compared to pure diffusion (7.0×), questioning generalization
Single-run results without error bars or confidence intervals, reducing confidence in improvement magnitudes especially for tasks with performance degradation
Missing computational overhead analysis: no explicit breakdown of CreditDecoding's own CPU/memory costs despite maintaining per-token credit tensors
Insufficient comparison with concurrent temporal-signal methods (e.g., Wang et al., 2025); primary baseline is Fast-dLLM alone
